title: Browser automation

html:
Browser automation

Browser is an optional rendered-reading and interactive skill on the selected Gateway. The ordinary Agent uses deterministic browser tools; there is no browser Agent, locator model, DOM summarizer or screenshot classifier. Web remains the separate lightweight public search/read skill. The optional Web Research Skill begins with Web and can request Browser separately when a named source needs rendered/session access. Selecting Web Research never grants Browser or changes Browser's operation effects and approvals. Browser is disabled in new capability selections by default. Existing saved selections remain authoritative. Enable Browser in the existing capability controls; individual tools show the selected Gateway's negotiated availability.

Installation and configuration

The standard Gateway installers install Playwright in the Gateway's Python environment, download its matching Chromium, and verify a local headless JavaScript render. Browser execution is enabled by default; no extra startup argument or environment variable is required. After updating an existing Gateway, restart it and refresh its metadata. Installation is an explicit operator action; imports and discovery never install packages or browser binaries.

./src/gateway_agent/install.sh
./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh

Use src/gateway_macos/install.sh / startup.sh on macOS and src/gateway_windows/install.ps1 / startup.ps1 on Windows. On apt-based Linux, setup also installs Chromium's OS dependencies unless AOR_SKIP_SYSTEM_DEPS=1, GATEWAY_SKIP_SYSTEM_DEPS=1, or AOR_INSTALL_SYSTEM_DEPS=0 is set. Other Linux distributions must provide compatible browser libraries. A failed download or launch fails installation rather than reporting a ready browser. Install and run under the same OS account, or configure the same accessible PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH for both.

Gateway setting Default and meaning
GATEWAY_BROWSER_ENABLED true; explicit false disables browser execution on this Gateway
GATEWAY_BROWSER_HEADLESS true; default for managed starts
GATEWAY_BROWSER_PROFILE_ROOT ~/.smto/browser; service creates a private managed child
GATEWAY_BROWSER_ALLOW_ATTACH false; allow explicit CDP attachment
GATEWAY_BROWSER_CDP_ENDPOINT Absent; operator-provided endpoint, never a tool argument or status field

Treat an authenticated CDP endpoint as a secret. Supply it through the Gateway environment, not ordinary application settings JSON. The setting is excluded from Settings serialization. No ports are scanned and no personal browser is relaunched or configured automatically.

The current backend is Chromium through Playwright, a standard runtime dependency. The browser extra remains accepted for compatibility. Linux managed headless and explicit CDP are exercised by local fixture tests. Windows/macOS use Playwright's Chromium APIs but require validation on those platforms. Firefox/WebKit, cloud browsers, extension attachment, stealth, CAPTCHA bypass and browser binary installation tools are absent. A headed session needs an interactive Gateway desktop and its display environment.

GET /capabilities includes browser_runtime. browser_status means diagnostics are supported, including when automation is unavailable. Other tags are browser_managed, browser_interact, browser_attach_cdp, browser_upload, browser_downloads, browser_screenshot, browser_headless and browser_headed. Missing package and missing Chromium binary have separate error identities. Controller OS and arbitrary configured capability tags cannot create backend support.

Sessions and discovery

The entry set is browser.status, browser.start, browser.tabs, browser.read_page. Discover the following sections for other operations. All IDs below use the browser. prefix.

Section Operations
browser.sessions status, start, stop, sessions, attach, detach
browser.tabs tabs, open_tab, activate_tab, close_tab
browser.navigation navigate, back, forward, reload, page_info
browser.read read_page, snapshot, find
browser.interact click, fill, type_text, press, select_option, check, scroll, wait_for
browser.files upload_file, downloads, wait_for_download, screenshot

Every session belongs to the conversation that created it on that Gateway. Exact opaque session and tab IDs prevent title-based targeting. Sessions live until explicit stop/detach or Gateway shutdown; they do not survive a Gateway restart. The service owns at most eight sessions and 32 tracked tabs per session. Calls serialize at the Gateway to avoid interleaved mutations.

A managed start defaults to Chromium, ephemeral persistence and the configured headless mode. profile is a short logical identifier, never an arbitrary directory. Persistent profiles require an SMTO ownership marker; an existing unmarked nonempty directory is rejected. Profiles are never copied from Chrome/Edge/Firefox defaults. stop retains persistent profiles and deletes only the temporary profile owned by that ephemeral session. POSIX directories use mode 0700. There is no profile-clear/delete tool.

An attached session has attached=true and uses only the operator's configured CDP endpoint. stop rejects it; detach disconnects without closing the externally owned context or process. Attachment is not equivalent to a newly managed session. When attachment is not configured, ask the operator to configure it or offer an explicitly separate managed session.

Semantic interaction and bounds

{"browser":"chromium","persistence":"ephemeral","headless":false,
 "initial_url":"https://support.example/"}

Use returned browser_session_id and tab_id for a read or find:

{"browser_session_id":"session_...","tab_id":"tab_...",
 "locator":{"role":"button","name":"Save","exact":true}}

Click a returned reference with the same session and tab:

{"browser_session_id":"session_...","tab_id":"tab_...","element_ref":"element_..."}

The alternative locator accepts exactly one of role (optionally name), label, text, test ID or placeholder. Exact matching and visible-only matching default to true. Actions require one match; zero and multiple matches have distinct errors. No CSS/XPath or arbitrary JavaScript argument exists. Main-frame semantic interaction is supported; iframe interaction is not.

References retain exact element handles, never a selector to be re-resolved later. DOM child/attribute/text changes and frame navigation invalidate the current generation. A new snapshot/find replaces the bounded reference working set. Never reuse a ref after a stale error; inspect again. This conservative behavior can invalidate refs on active SPAs more often than a human expects. Waits poll locally in the same operation, without additional Agent turns.

Reads exclude input values, hidden/script/style text and password values. Page text is bounded to 24,000 characters (default 8,000); snapshots/find to 200 elements (default 100); semantic candidate matching to 1,000. Metadata has independent bounds: 32 headings, 50 links/controls, three tables of at most 20 rows and ten cells per row. There is no full HTML result. A result has truncated when the selected projection exceeds its bounds. Envelopes are capped at 512 KiB. timeout_ms is 1–60,000, default 10,000, including waits and queue time.

Direct navigation accepts HTTP(S) only. Observed URLs omit userinfo, query and fragment; URL display also uses the shared redaction processor. Browser tools do not provide file: page reading or bypass the File skill's local-path boundary. Screenshots capture only the viewport (at most 16 million pixels), with input, textarea, select and editable fields masked. There is no periodic screenshot or DOM-content streaming.

Files, secrets and external content

Upload uses a regular absolute Gateway-local path and the existing no-follow file reader; it does not read the controller filesystem. Transfer a file from another Gateway using gateway.copy first. Uploads and artifact exports are capped at 16 MiB. A browser may receive a larger download into its browser-owned temporary area; export rejects it and deletes that browser download. The export cap is not a network traffic quota.

Downloads are observed only during explicit session operations and receive opaque IDs. Use wait_for_download or downloads with an exact download_id and as_artifact:true to await completion and export it. To wait for a newly observed download, use after_download_id when older downloads exist. Ambiguous selection never chooses the first download. At most 100 handles are retained per session. Download filenames remain untrusted metadata and never choose filesystem paths. Closing a session releases its browser temporary downloads; export requested outputs before stopping it.

Screenshots and exported downloads publish into the existing run artifact workspace. The normal collector transfers and registers durable artifact:// outputs on the controller. Binary content is never embedded in ordinary tool JSON. If collection fails, the normal artifact retry path applies without repeating the browser action.

This checkout uses literal Parameter Store values and optional redaction; it has no secure post-model substitution suitable for fill_secret. Accordingly, there is no fill_secret tool. fill, type_text and press reject password fields. Ask the user to log in directly in the headed browser and confirm completion through ordinary ask_user; never request the password in chat. No cookies, password database, authentication tokens, localStorage or sessionStorage export APIs exist. Existing ordinary input values are not returned.

Page text, labels, titles, URLs and filenames carry content_trust=untrusted_external_data. They are tool data, never system/developer instructions. Page requests to run commands or reveal secrets grant no authority. The normal Agent must use the user's request and existing permission policy. Shared transient-content minimization keeps browser arguments/page bodies out of diagnostics, portable history, automatic working-context capsules and Handoff; exact current-run tool evidence remains available. This is an architectural boundary, not a claim that arbitrary model reasoning can be mathematically guaranteed injection-proof.

Effects, cancellation and recovery

Sessions/list/status, page reads, snapshots/find, waits, download observation/export and screenshots are external reads. All other operations, including navigation, scrolling, activation and form actions, are external writes and use existing confirmation/permission machinery. Active Web Research has one scoped default-confirmation exception for its research Browser allowlist (session/tab management, navigation and ordinary interaction). Explicit Permission Policy Ask/Deny and deny mode, capability fences, unsafe-action checks, secret protections and unknown-effect replay restrictions still apply. Effect classes stay unchanged. Upload and attachment authority is not widened. No browser-specific approval store or classifier exists. See Web Research for method requirements and durable soft-allowance extension cards.

Transport routes are authenticated POST /browser/operation and POST /browser/cancel, with exact node checks on direct and outbound Gateways. Runtime execution identity and conversation/run scope are transport fields, not model arguments. Every request executes once; duplicate IDs are fenced. Identity-only fences are bounded to 8,192 per Gateway service lifetime and fail closed when full. Restart only after reconciling outstanding effects; existing durable native receipts continue to prohibit unknown mutation replay across restart.

Cancellation before dispatch proves non-execution. Once a mutation is submitted, cancellation, timeout or response loss can mean effect_unknown=true, executed=null, remote_effect_possible=true. These fields do not claim success or failure of the remote business action. Inspect page_info, snapshot and downloads to reconcile. Never click Submit again solely because the response was lost. Repeated Agent attempts remain blocked by the existing native unknown-effect machinery.

Canonical errors use browser_* error kinds and browser-* catalog slugs (also resolvable through dotted browser.* aliases). Examples: browser_backend_unavailable, browser_browser_binary_missing, browser_attach_not_configured, browser_element_stale, browser_element_ambiguous, browser_file_not_found_on_target, browser_secret_binding_unavailable, browser_operation_cancelled, and browser_operation_outcome_unknown. Error detail/manual links supply exact remediation; provider exception text, form contents and endpoint secrets are not copied into diagnostics.
